candidates.title: Restaurant website order alert

demandEvidence.chore: Notify the restaurant operator when a new website order is placed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A novice can test a single alert with synthetic or operator-entered orders; the source gives the requested outcome but no trigger setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small restaurant might pay for fewer missed order alerts, but the request proves neither buyer intent nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can pass one supplied order to a manually chosen alert channel; live website and WhatsApp connections are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A bounded alert loop could run after an order is supplied, but no source documents its trigger or delivery and a person must verify each alert.

evidence.reason: The literal request establishes an order-notification chore, but says nothing about frequency, inputs, trigger access, delivery setup, or payment.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (mean 4.8): the request supports exploring one order alert, but no implementation reference supports the live trigger or WhatsApp delivery, so the proposed small version is limited to synthetic or operator-supplied orders and remains unverified.

rejected.title: Auto-exist – Flow-state induction via raw mouse input (a biohacking experiment)
